tasks.prompt: Order the duties setup for the attendant during a confined space entry into a valve chamber.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: single entrant working in a force main valve chamber, attendant remains at the surface for the whole entry.

cards.label: Confirm the attendant has no other duties and is trained in the entry plan, communication method, and non-entry rescue
Start the entry log with entrant name, time in, and initial atmospheric readings, and confirm the permit is posted at the opening
Log the entrant out at exit, account for all tools and equipment, and close the entry record when the space is secured
Maintain continuous contact and atmospheric monitoring results relay, and order evacuation if readings or conditions change
Establish and test voice or radio communication between attendant and entrant before the entrant descends
Set up the retrieval system so the attendant can extract the entrant from outside without entering the space

tasks.explanation: The attendant role is set up before entry, not improvised during it. Communication and non-entry retrieval are proven first, the log and permit anchor the entry, and evacuation authority plus a logged exit close the attendant duties.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when continuous monitoring shows hydrogen sulfide rising during a wet well entry.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entrant is working in the wet well, attendant sees the hydrogen sulfide reading climbing toward the alarm limit on the remote display.

cards.label: Account for the entrant at the surface, assess their condition, and call emergency services if there are any symptoms or exposure concerns
Order the entrant to stop work and exit the space immediately when the alarm limit is reached or the trend is clearly rising to it
Record the readings, times, and actions on the permit and suspend the entry pending investigation
Have the supervisor review the cause, such as disturbed sludge, and revise the entry plan before any re-entry is authorized
Assist the exit from the surface using the retrieval system if the entrant cannot climb out unaided, without entering the space
Keep all workers clear of the opening and increase ventilation to the space from a safe position

tasks.explanation: Evacuation comes before everything when toxic gas rises, and rescue is by retrieval from outside, never by entry. Accounting for the entrant and medical caution follow, and the entry stays suspended until the plan is revised, because the same conditions would greet a second entrant.

tasks.prompt: Order the calibration and bump test routine for a four gas detector before a day of manhole entries.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: detector will be used for several confined space entries, calibration gas and a docking station are available at the shop.

cards.label: If any sensor fails the bump test, perform a full calibration and retest, or remove the detector from service if it still fails
Record the calibration or bump results, gas lot and expiry, and detector serial number in the equipment log
Inspect the detector, sensors, filters, pump, and sampling line for damage or blockage before powering on
Perform a bump test with the calibration gas and confirm each sensor responds and alarms within the required time
Issue the detector for the day with its sampling probe and confirm the crew knows the alarm setpoints and response
Power on in fresh air away from exhaust and allow the detector to complete its self test and fresh air zero

tasks.explanation: Physical inspection and a fresh air zero come before gas is applied. The bump test proves response, failure leads to calibration or removal from service, never to use anyway, and the log plus crew briefing complete the issue.

tasks.prompt: Order the closeout of a confined space entry after the work in a wet well is finished.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump work complete, entrant has exited, permit must be closed and the station returned to normal.

cards.label: Restore the space to service by removing isolations and lockouts in the planned order and restarting equipment as required
Confirm the entrant is out, is checked for any symptoms, and has signed the exit time on the entry log
Account for all tools, equipment, and materials so nothing is left in the space
Brief the supervisor on the completed work and any follow up defects or atmospheric concerns found
Remove ventilation, retrieval, and monitoring equipment and inspect it before returning it to storage
Close and sign the entry permit with final readings, work completed, and any issues noted, and file it as required

tasks.explanation: People and tools are accounted for before equipment comes out and isolations are removed. Restoring service follows the planned order, the permit is closed with the full record, and the supervisor briefing carries forward anything the next crew needs.

tasks.prompt: Order a non-entry rescue readiness check before a confined space entry begins.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entry into a deep manhole, rescue is planned as non-entry retrieval unless conditions require the fire service rescue team.

cards.label: Confirm the rescue plan in the entry permit names the method, the responders, and how emergency services will be called
Record the readiness check on the permit and do not authorize entry until every rescue item is confirmed in place
Confirm the attendant can operate the retrieval system alone and that a second worker or rescue contact is available as planned
Have the entrant don and adjust the harness and connect the lifeline before descending, and test the winch under light load
Anchor and position the retrieval system directly over the opening so the entrant can be raised vertically without dragging
Inspect the tripod, winch, harness, and lifeline for damage, correct assembly, and rated capacity for the entrant

tasks.explanation: The plan is confirmed on paper first, then the hardware is inspected and rigged for a straight vertical lift. The harness and winch are proven before descent, the attendant capability is confirmed, and entry is not authorized until rescue is genuinely ready.

tasks.prompt: Order the pre-entry testing for a manhole entry where the first test will be done after ventilation has started.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: deep trunk manhole with a history of hydrogen sulfide, blower is available and the permit requires testing before and during entry.

cards.label: Brief the entrant that ventilation and continuous monitoring must continue and that rising readings mean immediate exit
Test oxygen first, then flammables, then hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide, at the top, middle, and bottom of the space
Allow ventilation to run for the planned purge time based on the space volume and blower capacity
Confirm readings at every level are within entry limits with ventilation running and record them on the permit
Set up and start ventilation with the duct reaching the bottom of the manhole before testing for entry
Authorize entry and maintain continuous monitoring with readings logged at the intervals set in the permit

tasks.explanation: Ventilation precedes entry testing here because the space has a known hydrogen sulfide history and the entry condition is the ventilated condition. Testing at three levels in the standard gas order proves the whole space, and continuous monitoring protects the entry after authorization.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for testing a personal gas monitor alarm that activates at a manhole opening during a surface inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: no entry planned, a worker personal monitor alarms for hydrogen sulfide as the cover is lifted, both workers are at the surface.

cards.label: Note the gas and the reading if it can be read safely at a distance and record the time and location
Do not lean over or reach into the manhole and do not attempt to retrieve anything from inside
Move upwind and clear of the opening immediately and keep others away from the manhole
Record the alarm event, readings, and actions in the inspection log and flag the manhole as a known gas location
Notify the supervisor and treat any further work at the manhole as a confined space entry with a permit and full testing
Ventilate the manhole from the surface with a blower if it can be set up without exposure at the opening

tasks.explanation: Withdrawal upwind is immediate, because hydrogen sulfide can incapacitate in one breath at high concentration. Nothing is retrieved and no one leans in, ventilation is only from a safe position, and the location is escalated to permit entry status and flagged for every future crew.

tasks.prompt: Order a sewer flushing operation using a hydrant and flushing bag on a flat residential sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: low velocity flat grade sewer with sand and grit deposits, flushing from the upstream manhole toward the downstream manhole.

cards.label: Remove debris collected at the downstream manhole with the vacuum or by hand tools, and record the section cleaned and condition found
Repeat flushes as needed until the arriving water runs reasonably clear and the deposit has moved to the downstream manhole
Set up traffic control at both manholes and confirm communication between the two workers
Release the flush water in a controlled surge and watch the downstream manhole for the wave carrying debris
Install the flushing bag or hose at the upstream manhole and secure it so it cannot be lost into the pipe
Confirm the downstream manhole can receive the flush volume and check for any surcharge or blockage downstream first

tasks.explanation: The downstream must be proven able to receive the flush before water is released, or the flush creates a surcharge. Controlled surges move material to a capture point, debris is removed there rather than pushed further, and the record closes the job.

tasks.prompt: Order a high pressure jetting pass to clean a gravity sewer from the downstream manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: combination jet truck set up at the downstream manhole, cleaning the pipe upstream, standard rear facing jet nozzle.

cards.label: Advance the hose upstream under low pressure or with short bursts until it reaches the upstream manhole or the marked length
Increase to working pressure and pull the hose back slowly so the rear jets scour the pipe and carry debris back to the downstream manhole
Set up the truck and traffic control at the downstream manhole and confirm the section, pipe size, and length to be cleaned from the drawings
Select the nozzle for the pipe size and cleaning purpose and inspect hoses, fittings, and the pressure relief before pressurizing
Capture the debris at the downstream manhole with the vacuum, inspect the returning flow until it runs clear, and record the cleaning
Lower the nozzle into the downstream manhole and feed it into the pipe opening facing upstream, with the hose marked for distance

tasks.explanation: Setup, nozzle selection, and equipment checks precede pressurizing. The nozzle travels upstream first, and the cleaning happens on the slow pullback so debris is carried to the capture manhole, not pushed ahead, with vacuum capture and records finishing the pass.

tasks.prompt: Order the jetting response inside a pipe when the nozzle will not advance past a point partway upstream.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: jet hose stops advancing about halfway to the upstream manhole, operator suspects an obstruction or defect.

cards.label: Pull the hose back while jetting to clear loosened debris that may be piled in front of the nozzle
Mark the hose at the stopping distance and record the measured distance from the manhole for locating the problem
Reduce pressure and work the hose back and forth gently over a short distance to try to pass without forcing it
Try a different nozzle type suited to penetration only if the supervisor approves and the pipe condition allows
If the nozzle still will not pass, withdraw it fully and arrange CCTV inspection from either end to identify the obstruction
Record the stoppage distance, attempts made, and the CCTV follow up in the work order

tasks.explanation: Forcing a nozzle can damage the pipe or wedge the hose. Gentle working and debris clearing come first, the distance is measured and recorded because it locates the defect, and CCTV identification replaces blind force when the obstruction holds.

tasks.prompt: Order a mechanical rodding operation on a small diameter sewer with a partial root blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sectional rodding machine at the upstream access point, cleaning toward the downstream manhole where a second worker captures debris.

cards.label: Confirm the pipe size, length, and direction and set up the machine square to the access point with the guide hose in place
Withdraw and clean the rods, confirm flow is restored at the downstream manhole, and record the section, tools used, and debris found
Select the starting tool, such as a spear or auger head, suited to opening a pilot hole through the roots
When resistance is met, work the tool back and forth to cut through, then advance to the downstream manhole
Change to the larger finishing tool and pull back slowly to clear the remaining roots and debris toward the downstream capture point
Feed the rods in section by section with rotation, advancing steadily and adding sections as the tool moves downstream

tasks.explanation: Setup and a pilot tool come before feeding rods, because opening a hole precedes full clearing. Sections are added as the tool advances, the finishing tool works on pullback toward capture, and restored flow plus records prove the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the debris capture and disposal steps at the downstream manhole during a jetting operation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: jetting is bringing grit, rags, and grease chunks back to the downstream manhole where a vacuum hose is positioned.

cards.label: Continue jetting passes until the return water is clear and no further debris arrives at the manhole
Vacuum the manhole sump and benching clean and inspect the channel for remaining deposits
Monitor the returning flow and vacuum continuously so debris does not pass into the next pipe section
When heavy debris arrives, pause the pullback as needed to let the vacuum clear the manhole sump
Transport the collected material to the approved disposal point and record the estimated volume and disposal location
Position the vacuum hose in the downstream channel before jetting starts so debris is captured as it arrives

tasks.explanation: Capture is set up before cleaning starts, because debris that passes the manhole simply moves the problem downstream. Pausing for the vacuum keeps capture effective, clear return water signals completion, and approved disposal with records closes the loop.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleaning of a grease choked sewer section found during a blockage call.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 200 mm residential sewer heavily coated with grease, jet truck on site, downstream manhole accessible.

cards.label: Capture all grease and debris at the downstream manhole with the vacuum so it cannot reset downstream
Record the location as a grease hotspot with the date and amount removed, and recommend a cleaning frequency to the supervisor
Confirm full bore flow is restored by observing flow and, where available, a post cleaning camera check
Make repeated pullback passes, working from the downstream manhole upstream, until grease stops arriving in chunks
Confirm the extent of the grease by the flow condition and, if available, a quick camera or mirror check before choosing the nozzle
Select a jetting nozzle and pressure suited to grease removal and warm the line with initial low pressure passes if the equipment allows

tasks.explanation: Extent and nozzle choice come before jetting. Repeated pullbacks with capture remove grease in stages rather than pushing a plug ahead, restored flow is verified, and hotspot recording turns one call into preventive scheduling.

tasks.prompt: Order the root cutting operation in a sewer using a jet driven rotary cutter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV has confirmed root masses at several joints in a 250 mm sewer, cutter size must match the pipe.

cards.label: Select the cutter head sized just under the pipe internal diameter and inspect the skids, blades, and hose connections
Review the CCTV record to note the chainage and severity of each root mass before setting up
Cut at each root location with controlled passes, pulling back through the mass until the return flow shows roots are cleared
Vacuum the cut roots and debris at the downstream manhole after each section so fragments do not form a new blockage
Run a post cutting CCTV check of the treated joints and record the result and any joints needing rehabilitation referral
Set up at the downstream manhole and advance the cutter to the first root mass using the recorded distance and hose markings

tasks.explanation: The CCTV record targets the work, and correct sizing prevents pipe damage. Cutting is controlled and debris is captured after each section, because loose roots are a classic cause of a repeat blockage, and a post cutting camera run proves the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the decision sequence for cleaning before CCTV inspection of a problem sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a sewer with repeat blockages is booked for CCTV, the crew must decide how much cleaning is needed first.

cards.label: Check the flow and deposit level at both manholes to estimate how much material is in the pipe
Confirm the pipe is clean enough for the camera to travel and to see the walls by checking the return water clarity
If deposits are heavy, jet the section and capture debris at the downstream manhole before the camera run
Record the cleaning done, the inspection result, and any follow up cleaning or repair in the asset record
Run the CCTV inspection while the pipe is in the cleaned condition and record any remaining deposits honestly in the report
Review the blockage history and any previous CCTV to judge the likely deposits and defects in the section

tasks.explanation: History and a look in both manholes judge the need. Heavy deposits hide defects and stop cameras, so cleaning precedes inspection when needed, clarity confirms readiness, and the report records both the cleaning and what the camera actually saw.

tasks.prompt: Order a vacuum truck decant and disposal sequence at the end of a cleaning shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: combination unit is full of sewer debris and water after a day of jetting and manhole cleaning.

cards.label: Open the decant valve and drain the liquid portion slowly to the approved receiving point, controlling splashing and odour
Close and secure all valves, doors, and caps and check for leaks before leaving the facility
Wash down the tank, screens, and debris area and confirm no material remains to foul the next load or the road
Tilt or open the body as designed and discharge the solid debris into the approved containment or bin
Complete the disposal record with the source locations, estimated volumes, and the facility used
Return to the approved decant or disposal facility and position the truck as directed by the facility procedure

tasks.explanation: Disposal happens only at the approved facility in its sequence, liquid first, then solids, then washdown. Securing the truck prevents road spillage, and the disposal record links the waste to its sources for the cleaning program.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning sequence for a preventive sewer cleaning program visit to a street segment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program planner schedules next month cleaning for a group of high risk sewer sections.

cards.label: Assign the cleaning method for each section, such as jetting, rodding, or root cutting, based on its recorded problem
Issue the work orders with maps, pipe details, and the required downstream capture and disposal arrangements
After completion, update each asset record with the date, method, and debris found so the next ranking uses current data
Check access needs for each section, including easements, traffic control, and customer notification where driveways are affected
Group the highest ranked sections by area and manhole access so each crew day follows an efficient route
Rank candidate sections by blockage history, grease and root records, pipe age, and consequence of a backup or overflow

tasks.explanation: Risk ranking drives the program, not habit. Grouping, access, and method selection turn the ranking into workable crew days, and updating records after completion keeps the next cycle honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the post cleaning flow restoration check after clearing a sewer blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew has jetted a blocked residential sewer and the upstream manhole level is falling.

cards.label: Watch the upstream manhole until the backed up sewage has drained to the normal flow level
Check the downstream manhole to confirm the flow is arriving normally and no debris dam remains
Make one final light jetting pass if any doubt remains about loose debris in the section
Run water from an upstream source or confirm normal incoming flow passes freely through the cleaned section
Record the restored flow, the cause found, and the cleaning done before leaving the site
Check the affected customer service connection flow if the call involved a backup, with the customer informed

tasks.explanation: Restoration is proven, not assumed. The upstream level, free passage, and downstream arrival are checked in flow order, a final pass clears loose material that causes repeat calls, and the record captures the cause for the history file.

tasks.prompt: Order the washdown and inspection of jetting equipment at the end of the day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: jet truck returns to the yard after cleaning grease and grit from several sections.

cards.label: Check water tank, filters, oil, and fuel levels and refill or report as needed for the next shift
Record defects and servicing in the equipment log and notify the mechanic of anything affecting safe operation
Wash down the hose reel, nozzles, and truck surfaces at the yard wash area so debris does not dry on the equipment
Inspect the jet hose along its accessible length for cuts, abrasion, and damaged couplings and tag any defects
Drain or protect water lines and the pump against freezing when cold weather is expected
Clean and inspect each nozzle for blocked or worn jets and return serviceable nozzles to their storage positions

tasks.explanation: Washdown comes before inspection so damage is visible. Hose and nozzle condition are safety critical at jetting pressures, fluids and freeze protection ready the truck for the next shift, and the log passes defects to maintenance.

tasks.prompt: Order a bucket machine cleaning setup for a large trunk sewer with heavy grit, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two winch units set up at two manholes on a large diameter trunk sewer, buckets are pulled through the pipe to a capture manhole.

cards.label: Set up the winch units square over each manhole and pass the cable through the pipe using rods or a float line
Attach the bucket sized to the pipe and confirm the cable, pins, and connections are secure
Pull the bucket slowly toward the capture manhole, controlling the winch so the bucket loads without jamming
Empty each bucket load into the truck or container at the capture manhole and inspect what was removed
Repeat passes until buckets come through clean, then remove all equipment, restore flow, and record the material removed
Confirm the pipe size, length, and access at both manholes and that the flow can be managed during the work

tasks.explanation: Access and flow are confirmed before rigging. The cable must pass through before the bucket is attached, pulls are slow and controlled to avoid jams in a large main, and passes continue until clean buckets prove the section is clear.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup for cleaning a sewer on an easement behind houses with no road access.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manholes are in rear lot easements, the jet truck must stay on the street and run hose across private yards.

cards.label: Carry out the cleaning with a worker stationed at the remote manhole to guide the nozzle and watch the flow
Set up the truck on the street with traffic control and lay out and connect enough hose to reach the easement manhole
Confirm communication between the truck operator and the worker at the remote manhole before pressurizing
Confirm easement access rights and notify the affected residents of the work, timing, and yard access needed
Remove all hose and equipment, restore any disturbed yard areas, thank the residents, and record the access notes for future visits
Walk the hose route and agree the path with residents, protecting gardens, fences, and surfaces along the way

tasks.explanation: Access and notification come first on private land. The route is walked and agreed before hose is laid, communication is proven before pressure, and restoration plus recorded access notes make the next visit easier.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup and calibration steps before a CCTV inspection run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV truck set up at a manhole, camera will inspect a 300 mm sewer, distance accuracy matters for defect locations.

cards.label: Enter the header information, including manhole numbers, pipe size, material, direction, date, and operator
Inspect the camera, transporter, lights, and cable for damage and confirm the camera lens is clean
Set up the truck, traffic control, and cable reel at the starting manhole and confirm the section details from the drawings
Begin the run at the controlled survey speed with recording on and the distance counter running
Set the distance counter to zero at the pipe entry point with the camera positioned at the agreed reference
Lower the camera to the pipe, confirm picture quality, lighting, and focus in the pipe before starting the run

tasks.explanation: Section details and equipment condition come before calibration. Zeroing the counter at the entry reference is what makes every later defect location trustworthy, header data ties the video to the asset, and picture quality is proven before the survey starts.

tasks.prompt: Order the camera work during a CCTV run when a defect is found partway along the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator sees a cracked joint with roots at a service connection during a standard survey.

cards.label: Check the service connection at the same location for flow, roots, or damage and code it as a separate observation
Resume the survey at normal speed only after the defect record is complete
Hold a clear still image or pause long enough for the defect to be reviewed later
Record the distance reading, clock position, and defect description as the observation is coded
Pan and tilt or rotate the camera head to show the full extent of the defect around the pipe wall
Stop the camera advance at the defect and centre the defect in the picture

tasks.explanation: The survey pauses for defects, because a defect driven past is a defect lost. Centring, full viewing, coding with distance and clock position, and a reviewable image make the record usable, and connected services are coded separately before moving on.

tasks.prompt: Order the CCTV workflow when the camera cannot complete the run because of debris in the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: camera stops at a debris pile about two thirds along the section, the far manhole is accessible.

cards.label: If the section still cannot be completed, run the camera from the opposite manhole to cover the uninspected length
Record the distance reached, the reason for stopping, and the appearance of the obstruction in the survey record
Jet the section from the downstream manhole and capture the debris, then confirm the pipe is passable
Re-run the camera through the cleaned length to complete the survey of the remaining pipe
Close the survey record showing both runs, the cleaning done, and any length that remains uninspected and why
Withdraw the camera without forcing it and inspect the camera and cable for damage on recovery

tasks.explanation: The abandoned run is documented before withdrawal, because the stoppage itself is condition data. Cleaning and re-running follow, the reverse run is the fallback for full coverage, and the record honestly shows any gap that remains.

tasks.prompt: Order the defect coding and report completion steps after a CCTV survey shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator has completed four surveys and must finish the records before the data leaves the truck.

cards.label: Flag the most severe defects for supervisory review and mark any surveys that were incomplete with the reason
Save and back up the video and database files in the project structure with the standard file naming
Transfer the completed package to the asset management system and note any sections needing cleaning or repair work orders
Review each video and confirm every observation has a distance, clock position where relevant, and a defect code
Generate the inspection reports and confirm the photographs match the coded observations
Check the header data on each survey against the drawings and correct any manhole, size, or material errors

tasks.explanation: Coding is checked against the video first, then headers against the drawings, because both errors corrupt the asset record. Severe defects are flagged, files are backed up before reports are generated, and transfer plus work order notes put the results to work.

tasks.prompt: Order a lateral launch camera inspection from a mainline sewer, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mainline camera with a lateral launch unit will inspect a service connection suspected of root intrusion.

cards.label: Confirm the lateral direction and the address it serves from the drawings and the connection position
Advance to the recorded problem distance or the property line limit, coding roots, joints, and defects as they are seen
Withdraw the lateral camera fully into the mainline unit before moving the mainline camera again
Feed the lateral camera into the connection slowly, watching for bends, traps, or a backwater valve that could stop it
Complete the mainline survey to the target service connection and position the launch camera facing the lateral opening
Record the lateral survey with the address, distance reached, and findings linked to the mainline survey record

tasks.explanation: The mainline run positions the launcher first. Direction and address are confirmed before entering private plumbing, the lateral camera is fully recovered before the main unit moves, and the record links the lateral findings to the right property and mainline survey.

tasks.prompt: Order the quality check of CCTV data before it is accepted into the asset system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reviewer checks a contractor CCTV submission for a group of sewer sections.

cards.label: Confirm every submitted section has a video file, a database record, and a report that match each other
Play samples of the video and confirm picture quality, lighting, and survey speed allow the walls to be assessed
Check distances against the known section lengths and flag surveys where the counter error is more than the allowed tolerance
Accept passing surveys into the asset system and update each pipe record with its condition and inspection date
Reject or return surveys that fail the checks with the reasons recorded for the contractor
Compare coded defects against the video at several observations to confirm the coding matches what is visible

tasks.explanation: Completeness comes before quality sampling. Distance accuracy and coding accuracy are checked against the video itself, failures are returned with reasons rather than silently accepted, and accepted data updates the asset record that drives future work.

tasks.prompt: Order an emergency CCTV inspection to locate a blockage in a sewer with a backup in progress.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew needs the blockage location quickly to choose between jetting, rodding, and excavation.

cards.label: Withdraw the camera and give the measured location and obstruction type to the cleaning or repair crew
Run the camera upstream from the flowing end so the lens stays in clear water as long as possible
Record the emergency survey, the location given, and the action taken in the work order the same day
Note the type of obstruction if visible, such as roots, grease, debris, or a collapsed section
Advance until the camera reaches the blockage or the water becomes too deep and dirty to see, and record that distance
Set up at the downstream manhole where flow is present and confirm the direction and length of the affected section

tasks.explanation: Starting from the flowing downstream end keeps the camera in visible water longest. The measured distance and obstruction type are the products the response crew needs, and same day recording preserves the emergency findings for the asset history.

tasks.prompt: Order the installation planning for a temporary flow monitor in a trunk sewer manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: area velocity monitor will record for eight weeks to support a capacity study, site is a deep manhole on a collector sewer.

cards.label: Select the site for straight, uniform flow with no junction turbulence, drops, or backwater effects at the sensor location
Program the logger with the pipe dimensions, logging interval, and site identification before going to site for installation
Record the site details, photographs, and access notes in the monitoring plan so any crew can service the site
Visit the site to measure pipe size, shape, and silt depth and to confirm safe access and a mounting position
Schedule the installation and the first data check date in the monitoring program calendar
Plan the installation visit with traffic control, confined space arrangements if entry is needed, and the required tools and bands

tasks.explanation: Hydraulics decide the site, because a monitor in turbulent or backed up flow produces data no one can use. Measurements and programming precede the install visit, and documented site details plus a scheduled first check protect the whole study.

tasks.prompt: Order the installation of an area velocity flow sensor in a sewer manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sensor and logger are programmed, crew installs on a mounting band in the invert of a 450 mm pipe, entry follows the confined space plan where required.

cards.label: Take a manual depth measurement at a recorded time to compare with the logger reading before leaving
Record the installation details, sensor serial numbers, zero references, and the comparison reading in the site file
Set up traffic control, ventilation, and atmospheric testing and complete the entry arrangements for the manhole
Connect the sensor to the logger, confirm live depth and velocity readings respond to the flow, and secure the logger in the manhole
Measure and record the pipe internal dimensions and the silt or sediment depth at the sensor location
Mount the sensor band in the invert at the marked position with the sensor centred and the cable routed clear of the flow path

tasks.explanation: Safety setup comes first, then the physical measurements the logger calculations depend on. Live readings prove the sensor works in place, a manual comparison anchors the data, and the site file records everything a later analyst needs.

tasks.prompt: Order the first data check visit two weeks after a flow monitor is installed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: technician downloads the first data and checks the monitor is producing believable depth and velocity.

cards.label: Record the check results and any adjustments in the site file and report any data concerns to the study lead
Plot or review the depth and velocity traces for a normal daily pattern with morning and evening peaks
Check battery or power status and replace or plan replacement so the remaining study period is covered
Check the sensor for fouling, silt burial, or displacement and clean or reseat it if the readings suggest a problem
Download the data and confirm there are no gaps and the clock and logging interval are correct
Take a manual depth reading at a recorded time during the visit and compare it with the logged depth for that time

tasks.explanation: Data integrity is checked before the site work, because gaps and clock errors invalidate a study quietly. The daily pattern and a manual depth comparison test believability, fouling and power are the common physical causes of bad data, and the site file carries the verdict.

tasks.prompt: Order the data quality review for a flow monitoring study before the results are used.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: eight weeks of data from three monitors will support infiltration and inflow analysis.

cards.label: Review depth and velocity scatter and hydrographs for drift, flat lining, spikes, and sensor fouling periods
Document the data quality decisions, excluded periods, and corrections in the study report so the analysis can be audited
Compare manual check readings with logged values and note any offset or drift correction that is justified
Calculate average dry weather flow and wet weather response for each site using the cleaned data only
Separate dry weather days from wet weather days using the rainfall record for each site
Confirm the data sets are complete for the study period and align the logger clocks with the rain gauge record

tasks.explanation: Completeness and time alignment come before interpretation, because a one hour clock error ruins a rain response comparison. Quality review and justified corrections precede any calculation, and documenting exclusions makes the study defensible.

tasks.prompt: Order the pairing of rainfall data with flow data for a wet weather response check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: analyst checks how one monitored sewershed responded to a storm last week.

cards.label: Follow the flow recession after the rain ends to see how long the elevated response continues
Align the flow and rainfall records to the same time base and time zone before comparing them
Identify the pre-storm dry weather flow pattern for the same hours of day
Confirm the rain gauge is in or near the sewershed and its record covers the storm with no gaps
Record the storm depth, peak response, and recession behaviour in the sewershed wet weather file
Measure the flow rise after the rain starts, the peak flow, and the time from rain start to peak

tasks.explanation: Gauge relevance and time alignment come first, because mismatched clocks create false lag times. Baseline, rise, peak, and recession describe the response in time order, and the filed record builds the sewershed history used for rehabilitation priorities.

tasks.prompt: Order the removal of a temporary flow monitor at the end of a study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study is complete, sensor and logger must come out and the final data must be secured.

cards.label: Confirm the download is complete and backed up before authorizing removal
Clean the equipment, check it into the equipment store, and report any damage for repair before the next deployment
Inspect the sensor and cable for damage or heavy fouling and note anything that could have affected the last data
Close the site file with the removal date, final data location, and equipment condition notes
Download the final data at the office connection or on site before disturbing the installation
Set up traffic control and entry arrangements and remove the logger, sensor, band, and cables from the manhole

tasks.explanation: Data is secured before hardware is touched, because a disturbed installation cannot be re-measured. Removal follows the same safety setup as installation, equipment condition is recorded while the evidence is fresh, and the closed site file completes the study trail.

tasks.prompt: Order the comparison of dry weather and wet weather flows to estimate extraneous flow in a sewershed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: analyst has cleaned flow and rainfall data for a residential sewershed with suspected infiltration and inflow.

cards.label: Identify the wet weather events and calculate the peak and total flow for each event
Estimate the base infiltration component from the minimum night flows on dry days
Calculate the average dry weather flow and its daily pattern from rain free days in the record
Subtract the matching dry weather flow from the wet weather flow to estimate the rain dependent portion
Compare the rain dependent portion with the rainfall depth for each event to rank the events consistently
Present the extraneous flow estimates with the data quality notes for use in rehabilitation planning

tasks.explanation: Dry weather flow is the baseline for every later subtraction, so it is calculated first. Wet weather response, rain normalization, and night flow infiltration follow in analysis order, and the estimates are only presented with their quality notes attached.

tasks.prompt: Order a night flow isolation study to locate infiltration in a residential sewershed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew works between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m. when sanitary flow is lowest, isolating subareas by plugging or measuring at key manholes.

cards.label: Begin at the outlet and record the total night flow for the whole sewershed as the starting reference
Record the results and mark the high flow subareas for manhole inspection, smoke or dye follow up, and CCTV
Calculate the flow per length of sewer for each subarea and identify the areas with unusually high night flow
Brief the crew on the route, the measurement method, safety and traffic arrangements, and the recording sheet for each manhole
Plan the isolation sequence from the outlet manhole upstream, listing each branch that will be measured or plugged in turn
Isolate or measure each branch in upstream order and record the flow contributed by each subarea

tasks.explanation: Night flow work runs from the outlet upstream so each branch contribution is measured against the total. Per length comparison finds the leaky subareas, and the follow up methods are targeted where the numbers point, not spread evenly.

tasks.prompt: Order a smoke testing program day in a residential area, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew will smoke test several streets to find inflow connections, residents must be protected and informed.

cards.label: Introduce smoke and walk the section watching for smoke from roof leaders, catch basins, yard drains, cleanouts, and ground defects
Remove the equipment, restore normal conditions, and file the defect list for dye confirmation or repair follow up
Photograph and record each smoke location with the address or asset reference and the likely connection type
Notify residents in advance with the date, the purpose, what to expect, and instructions to pour water into dry traps and drains
Notify the fire department and the municipal contact centre on the day so smoke reports are expected and handled
Isolate the test section between manholes and set up the smoke blower sealed at the starting manhole

tasks.explanation: Notification protects residents and prevents false fire alarms, so it precedes any smoke. The section is isolated and sealed before smoke is introduced, observations are recorded with locations while visible, and the filed list drives confirmation work.

tasks.prompt: Order a dye test to confirm a suspected cross connection, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: smoke testing suggested a roof leader or drain connects to the sanitary sewer at one property, dye will confirm it.

cards.label: If no dye appears in a reasonable time, check the storm sewer or other outlet before concluding the connection does not exist
Introduce the dyed water into the suspected drain at a controlled rate while the watcher observes the manhole
If dye appears, record the travel time, the colour intensity, and photograph the dyed flow in the manhole
Set a watcher with communication at the downstream sanitary manhole before any dye is introduced
Obtain the owner permission and arrange access, and confirm which fixture or drain will be dyed and where it should appear if connected
Record the confirmed or unconfirmed result with the address and notify the follow up program for correction of confirmed connections

tasks.explanation: Permission and a posted watcher come before dye, because an unwatched test proves nothing. Travel time and photographs make the confirmation solid, the storm outlet is checked before a negative conclusion, and confirmed connections go forward for correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation of high flows at a lift station after heavy rain to separate inflow from normal flow growth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: station run times doubled during a storm and stayed high for a day, supervisor wants the likely sources ranked.

cards.label: Record the storm response findings in the sewershed file so the next storm can be compared
Inspect key manholes in the suspected areas for surcharge marks, displaced covers, and active infiltration while conditions are still wet
Rank the likely sources by the evidence found and propose targeted smoke, dye, or night flow work for each
Check for surface inflow points such as manholes in ditches or low areas that could have been submerged during the storm
Review which subareas in the sewershed are low lying, have combined connections, or have a history of inflow defects
Compare the station flows and run times for the storm with dry weather days at the same station

tasks.explanation: Flow comparison proves the size of the problem before field work. History focuses the inspection, wet conditions show active sources that dry inspections miss, and ranking with targeted follow up turns one storm into a work plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the follow up workflow after smoke testing identifies multiple inflow defects on one street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: smoke day found roof leaders, a yard drain, and two defective cleanout caps on one street.

cards.label: Prioritize the defects by likely flow contribution, with direct roof and area drains ahead of minor cap defects
Update the sewershed record with defects found, corrected, and outstanding for the next analysis
Confirm the highest priority connections with dye testing where the smoke evidence was not conclusive
Compile the defect list with addresses, photographs, and the type of each connection found
Issue the correction notices or work orders according to the municipal program for private and public side defects
Schedule a re-test or flow check after corrections to confirm the inflow was actually removed

tasks.explanation: A compiled, prioritized list comes before action. Dye confirmation protects against ordering corrections on weak evidence, notices and work orders follow the program rules, and re-testing proves the program removed flow rather than just paper.

tasks.prompt: Order the check of a foundation drain or sump pump connection suspected of adding inflow to the sanitary sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one property shows a strong clear water signal in the lateral during rain, crew will investigate with the owner present.

cards.label: With the owner, locate the sump pump discharge and foundation drain arrangements and note where each discharges
Record the visit, evidence, and agreed actions in the property and sewershed files
Review the lateral inspection and flow evidence for the property and arrange the visit with the owner
Run the sump pump or introduce dyed water as agreed and watch the sanitary cleanout or downstream manhole for response
Explain the finding to the owner and provide the municipal requirements and timelines for correction if a connection is confirmed
Confirm whether clear water reaches the sanitary system and record the path it takes

tasks.explanation: Evidence review and owner arrangement come first. Locating the plumbing precedes any test, the test confirms the path, the owner hears the finding with the correction requirements, and both files record what was agreed.

tasks.prompt: Order the rehabilitation priority workflow for sewers with confirmed infiltration from CCTV and night flow data.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program lead must rank ten candidate sections for next year lining and sealing budget.

cards.label: Rank the sections by infiltration rate per length and by the severity of the structural defects found
After construction, schedule post rehabilitation flow monitoring to verify the reduction achieved
Prepare the recommended program with costs and expected flow reduction for supervisor approval
Combine the night flow rates, CCTV defect records, and manhole infiltration observations for each candidate section
Check each top ranked section for access, bypass needs, and conflicts with planned road or utility work
Group adjacent high ranked sections into project packages that can be built in one contract

tasks.explanation: Combined evidence ranks the sections, because flow alone can mislead and defects alone do not measure leakage. Buildability and packaging turn a ranking into a program, approval precedes construction, and verification monitoring proves the money worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the post rehabilitation flow check for a sewershed where mains and manholes were sealed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: rehabilitation finished last month, the same monitor location used before the work is available again.

cards.label: Compare the before and after results and calculate the reduction in infiltration and storm response
Report the verified reduction and the remaining sources in the sewershed file and program summary
Calculate the dry weather and night flows using the same method as the pre rehabilitation analysis
Reinstall the flow monitor at the same location and with the same setup used for the pre rehabilitation study
Investigate any area that did not improve for missed sources such as private side laterals
Record at least several dry weather days and, if possible, a rain event comparable to the pre work record

tasks.explanation: Same location, same setup, and same method are what make the comparison fair. Dry and wet results are calculated before conclusions, unimproved areas are investigated rather than averaged away, and the verified reduction is reported with what remains.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a manhole found with a displaced cover in a low area after a storm, as an inflow source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: resident reports a manhole cover ajar in a ditch area after heavy rain, flow at the downstream station was high.

cards.label: Attend and protect the location with barriers if the open or displaced cover is a hazard to the public
Arrange any needed frame sealing, cover replacement with a sealed or bolted cover, or grade adjustment as a work order
Record the location as a confirmed inflow point in the sewershed file with the storm date and evidence
Inspect inside the manhole for debris carried in by inflow and for damage to the benching or channel
Reseat or replace the cover correctly and check the frame for damage or a poor fit that allowed displacement
Photograph the cover, frame, and surrounding drainage and note whether surface water is entering the manhole

tasks.explanation: Public protection and evidence come before reseating, because the displaced position is the proof of the inflow path. Frame condition decides the lasting fix, the inside is checked for carried in damage, and the sewershed file gains a confirmed source for the program.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a residential sewer backup call where sewage is in a basement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: homeowner reports sewage backing up through a basement floor drain, municipal crew responds to determine if the main is blocked.

cards.label: Confirm the municipal main condition after any cleaning by observing free flow at both manholes
If the main is surcharged or blocked, set up cleaning from the downstream manhole and clear the blockage toward the capture point
Check the upstream and downstream manholes on the municipal main to determine whether the main is flowing or surcharged
If the main is flowing freely, advise the homeowner the problem is likely in the private lateral and explain the next steps under municipal policy
Record the caller details, address, time, and whether neighbours are affected, and advise the homeowner to avoid water use and keep clear of the sewage
Complete the call record with the findings, actions, and advice given, and flag any main defect for follow up inspection

tasks.explanation: Call details and the main condition decide everything, because cleaning a clear main does not help a lateral blockage. The manholes are checked before equipment is committed, cleaning runs from downstream with capture, and the record separates municipal from private responsibility clearly.

tasks.prompt: Order the clearing of a mainline blockage where the upstream manhole is surcharged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 200 mm main blocked, sewage is near the top of the upstream manhole, downstream manhole is accessible and flowing.

cards.label: Set up the jet truck at the downstream manhole with vacuum capture ready before disturbing the blockage
Protect the area and check for any overflow or basement risk at nearby properties and notify the supervisor of the surcharge condition
When the blockage releases, control the surge by continuing to vacuum at the downstream manhole until the upstream level falls to normal
Advance the jet nozzle upstream into the blockage slowly, working in short advances so released material does not overwhelm the capture
Make cleaning passes until the section runs clear and inspect the recovered debris for the cause, such as roots, grease, or wipes
Record the cause, debris, and cleaning done, and arrange CCTV follow up if the cause suggests a structural defect

tasks.explanation: Risk and capture are set before the blockage is touched, because releasing a surcharge without capture trades a blockage for an overflow. Controlled advances manage the surge, debris identifies the cause, and CCTV follows when the cause points to the pipe itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a sanitary sewer overflow reaching a roadside ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sewage is overflowing from a surcharged manhole and flowing toward a ditch that leads to a creek.

cards.label: Protect public safety at the site and notify the supervisor immediately so regulatory notification can begin without delay
Contain the overflow as close to the source as possible with berms, sandbags, or a vacuum truck to keep sewage out of the ditch and creek
Complete the overflow report with times, estimated volume, cause, actions, and notifications, and file it the same day
Clear the cause if it is a blockage, using downstream cleaning with capture, or arrange bypass pumping if the cause cannot be cleared quickly
Notify or support notification of the Spills Action Centre and the local health and environmental contacts as directed under Ontario spill reporting practice
Clean and disinfect the affected area, recover pooled sewage with the vacuum truck, and arrange sampling if directed

tasks.explanation: Safety and immediate supervisory notification start the clock for regulatory reporting. Containment near the source protects the creek before cause removal, notifications follow Ontario spill practice, and cleanup plus a same day report with volume and cause complete the response.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleanup sequence after an overflow on a grassed and paved area is contained.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: overflow has stopped, pooled sewage remains on a paved laneway and the grass beside it, no watercourse was reached.

cards.label: Remove contaminated debris and, on grass, restrict access and apply the disinfection or liming practice directed by the supervisor
Inspect storm drains and catch basins nearby and clean any that received sewage during the event
Record the cleanup method, areas treated, and any sampling results in the overflow file before closing the site
Wash down the paved area to a controlled collection point and vacuum the wash water rather than letting it reach a storm drain
Confirm the cause is corrected and flows are normal so cleanup will not be undone by another overflow
Recover all pooled liquid and solids with the vacuum truck, starting from the furthest extent back toward the source

tasks.explanation: Cleanup starts only when the cause is fixed. Recovery works from the outside back so contamination is not spread, wash water is captured rather than moved to the storm system, nearby storm assets are checked, and the file records the full treatment.

tasks.prompt: Order the documentation and follow up after a sewer overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: overflow is cleaned up, the office record and the prevention follow up remain to be completed.

cards.label: Complete the overflow report with the start and stop times, location, estimated volume, cause, and weather conditions
Record the cleanup actions, disposal, and any sampling taken with its results when received
Attach the notification record showing who was advised and when, including the Spills Action Centre reference if one was given
Raise the follow up work for the cause, such as CCTV inspection, cleaning frequency change, or a repair work order
Have the supervisor review and sign the file, and close it only when sampling results and follow up work orders are attached
Enter the event in the overflow history for the asset so repeat locations become visible in program planning

tasks.explanation: The report captures facts while they are fresh, notifications are evidenced rather than asserted, and cause follow up is raised as real work. History entry makes repeats visible, and supervisory sign off waits until results and work orders are actually attached.

tasks.prompt: Order a grease interceptor inspection at a food service establishment under the FOG program, at an awareness level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspector visits a restaurant to check its grease interceptor maintenance under the municipal sewer use program.

cards.label: Review the establishment record for the interceptor size, required cleaning frequency, and past compliance before the visit
Record the measurements, photographs where permitted, and the agreed actions in the FOG program file and schedule any re-inspection
Introduce the inspection to the operator, explain its purpose, and arrange safe access to the interceptor
Explain any non-compliance found, the required correction, and the timeline, and provide the program information sheet
Check the cleaning records and receipts the operator keeps and compare them with the condition found
Open the interceptor and measure the grease and solids layers against the allowable depth in the program requirements

tasks.explanation: The record sets the expectation before the visit. Measurement against the program limit is the core evidence, records are compared with reality, the operator hears the correction and timeline directly, and a scheduled re-inspection makes the follow up real.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning of root treatment for a sewer with recurring root blockages at the same joints.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three blockages in two years at the same joints in a clay pipe street, cleaning alone is not holding.

cards.label: Assess with the supervisor whether chemical root treatment, joint sealing, or lining is the right next step for this pipe and its remaining life
Review the blockage history and CCTV records to confirm the joints, severity, and whether the pipe is otherwise sound
Set a follow up CCTV inspection date to check regrowth and treatment effect
Record the decision, treatment, and inspection plan in the asset record so the cycle is managed rather than rediscovered at the next blockage
Cut and clean the roots thoroughly so any treatment or lining can reach the joint surfaces
Schedule the chosen treatment in the season and conditions the product or method requires, with customer notification if access is needed

tasks.explanation: History and CCTV confirm the target before money is spent. Thorough cutting prepares any treatment, the choice weighs pipe condition and remaining life, and a planned regrowth check plus a complete asset record turn repeat emergencies into managed maintenance.

tasks.prompt: Order the setting of a preventive cleaning frequency for a grease hotspot section.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a section below several restaurants needs a scheduled cleaning interval instead of emergency calls.

cards.label: Inspect or camera check the section after a thorough cleaning to establish the clean baseline condition
After each scheduled cleaning, record the grease amount found as light, moderate, or heavy for that interval
Add the section to the cleaning program with its method, access notes, and downstream capture requirements
Adjust the interval based on the recorded findings, lengthening it only when repeated light findings support the change
Review the blockage and cleaning history to find how quickly grease rebuilt to a problem level after the last thorough cleaning
Set the initial interval shorter than the observed rebuild time so cleaning happens before flow is restricted

tasks.explanation: The rebuild rate from history sets the science of the interval. A clean baseline and an interval shorter than the failure time prevent backups, recorded findings at each visit provide the evidence, and intervals change on data, not on hope.

tasks.prompt: Order the escalation workflow for a sewer section with its third blockage in six months.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: same section has blocked three times, each time cleared by jetting, no CCTV has been done yet.

cards.label: Run CCTV through the section and code all defects, deposits, and service connection conditions
Compile the three call records and compare the cause, debris, and exact location reported each time
Clean the section thoroughly with debris capture so it is ready for a diagnostic inspection
Decide the corrective action from the evidence, such as root treatment, grease program changes, point repair, or lining
Record the escalation decision in the asset history and set a review date to confirm the action was completed
Raise the work order or program change with a priority that reflects the blockage frequency and backup risk

tasks.explanation: Comparing the three calls first shows whether it is truly the same problem. Cleaning prepares a real diagnosis, CCTV provides it, the corrective action follows the evidence rather than another jetting visit, and a review date keeps the escalation from stalling.

tasks.prompt: Order an odour complaint investigation at a residential street served by a gravity sewer and a nearby lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: resident reports a rotten egg odour in the evenings, source could be a manhole, the lift station, or a private plumbing issue.

cards.label: Record the complaint details, times of day, weather, and exact locations where the odour is noticed
Visit at a time matching the complaint pattern and check the street manholes and the lift station exterior for odour strength and direction
Advise the complainant of the findings and actions and record the investigation and outcome in the complaint file
Use a gas detector at manhole openings where odour is present to check for hydrogen sulfide, without entry
If a municipal source is confirmed, arrange the corrective action such as wet well cleaning, vent repair, or odour control adjustment
Check the lift station for sources such as a vent, a grease mat in the wet well, or long detention causing septicity

tasks.explanation: The complaint pattern directs the visit timing. Municipal sources are checked from the street to the station, detector readings confirm hydrogen sulfide rather than relying on noses, corrective action follows a confirmed source, and the complainant plus the file both receive the outcome.

tasks.prompt: Order the odour control check at a lift station with a chemical feed system for sulfide control.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: station doses a sulfide control chemical, odour complaints have increased downstream of the station.

cards.label: Review the chemical feed records, tank levels, and dosing rates for the period when complaints increased
Check the chemical tank, pump, tubing, and injection point for leaks, blockages, or an empty tank that stopped dosing
Check detention conditions in the wet well and force main, such as low flows or long pump off times, that increase sulfide generation
Confirm the dosing pump output by a drawdown or calibration check against the set rate
Restore correct dosing, record the fault found, and set a follow up odour check date with the complainant area
Measure hydrogen sulfide at the force main discharge point if equipment is available and compare with past readings

tasks.explanation: Records and the physical feed system come first, because most odour control failures are feed failures. Output is proven by measurement, detention explains generation changes, discharge readings verify the effect, and a dated follow up closes the complaint loop.

tasks.prompt: Order the follow up inspection for corrosion where hydrogen sulfide odour is confirmed at a discharge manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: force main discharges into a gravity manhole, strong odour is present and the concrete above the flow line looks soft and eroded.

cards.label: Photograph and measure the extent of the corrosion and compare with any previous inspection photographs
Raise a rehabilitation or protective coating work order with a priority based on the measured loss of section
Check the upstream force main detention and sulfide control to identify actions that reduce gas release at this manhole
Confirm the hydrogen sulfide presence with a detector at the opening and record the reading and conditions
