Add the manhole to the corrosion watch list with a re-inspection interval in the asset record
Inspect the manhole crown, walls above the flow line, and pipe soffit from the surface for corrosion loss, exposed aggregate, or soft concrete

tasks.explanation: Gas confirmation and visual corrosion evidence together make the case. Comparison with past photographs measures the rate, upstream sulfide control reduces the cause, rehabilitation priority follows the measured damage, and the watch list keeps a slow failure visible.

tasks.prompt: A residential street reports slow drains at three homes, all downstream of one large maple tree.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario gravity sewer, 200 mm clay pipe. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV in the affected reach shows fine white root hairs entering at two joints near the maple tree.
Flow upstream of the tree reach is normal and the pipe there is clear on CCTV.
Jetting clears the line for two weeks, then slow drains return at the same three homes.
No grease or wipes are seen on CCTV in this reach, only roots at the joints.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A grease buildup is causing the recurring partial blockage
The whole street sewer has collapsed and lost its grade
A single home lateral is blocked and the main is clear
Roots entering at joints near the tree are causing the recurring partial blockage

inference.explanation: Roots are seen entering at joints exactly where problems recur, upstream is clear, and regrowth after jetting explains the two week return. No grease is seen, a collapse would not clear with jetting, and three homes share the reach.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms roots as the recurring cause before a repair is chosen?

options.label: Restaurant grease discharge records for the street
Water use records for the three homes
CCTV log with joint locations and root regrowth noted at the same joints on a follow up run

nextClue.explanation: A follow up CCTV log showing regrowth at the same joints confirms a living root source rather than a one time debris event.

clueText.nc-a: Grease records do not explain roots seen on camera or regrowth at fixed joints.
clueText.nc-b: Home water use does not locate a blockage inside a shared sewer reach.
clueText.nc-c: Follow up CCTV shows fresh root hairs at the same two joints, with the rest of the reach clear.

tasks.prompt: Sewage backs up into a basement during dry weather on a street with mature trees and old clay pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario street, dry weather backup. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The backup occurs in dry weather with no rain in the previous five days.
A root ball removed by rodding is mostly fine roots with a small amount of soil.
CCTV shows a root mass at a joint 12 m downstream of the affected home.
Neighbours on the same reach report the same slow drainage, homes on the next street do not.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: One toilet in the affected home is faulty and causing the backup
The treatment plant is backing flow up into the street
A root mass in the shared main is restricting flow for the whole reach
Rainfall inflow through roof leaders is surcharging the sewer

inference.explanation: Dry weather rules out rainfall inflow, several homes on one reach are affected, and a root mass is located in the main downstream of them. A single fixture fault cannot affect neighbours.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best separates a main root blockage from a lateral problem?

options.label: Toilet repair invoice for the affected home
Dye test and CCTV from the downstream manhole showing the root mass in the main while laterals run clear
Rain gauge records for the backup day

nextClue.explanation: Locating the mass in the main with clear laterals separates a shared main blockage from a single lateral fault.

clueText.nc-a: A toilet invoice cannot explain neighbours with the same symptoms on the same reach.
clueText.nc-b: CCTV from the downstream manhole shows the root mass in the main and dye from each lateral arrives freely.
clueText.nc-c: The day was dry, so rain records cannot explain a dry weather backup.

tasks.prompt: A sewer reach needs jetting every month, always at the same location, while nearby reaches stay clear for years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario maintenance records for one sewer reach. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Work orders cluster at one 30 m reach beside a row of willow trees.
CCTV shows roots at three joints in that reach and no defects in the pipe barrels.
After chemical root treatment, the jetting interval stretches from one month to eleven months.
Jetting returns from other reaches contain grit and debris, returns from this reach contain roots.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The jetting crew is skipping this reach on each visit
Living roots at the joints are regrowing into this reach between cleanings
Grit is accumulating because the reach has no grade
Residents are flushing wipes that collect at this reach

inference.explanation: Returns contain roots, CCTV shows roots at joints with sound barrels, and root treatment greatly extends the interval. Grit, wipes, and skipped work do not match the returns or the treatment response.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best proves the regrowth pattern for planning the next treatment?

options.label: Dated CCTV stills from the same joints showing root mass increasing between treatments
Crew timesheets for the jetting truck
Grit tonnage records at the treatment plant

nextClue.explanation: Dated images at fixed joints showing growth over time prove regrowth and set the retreatment interval.

clueText.nc-a: Stills eight months apart show the root mass at joint two growing from light hairs to a dense mat.
clueText.nc-b: Timesheets show attendance, not what is growing inside the pipe.
clueText.nc-c: Plant grit tonnage is system wide and cannot locate growth in one reach.

tasks.prompt: Flow in a 250 mm sewer is slow and CCTV shows a white fibrous mass hanging from the top of the pipe at one joint.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV inspection of a 250 mm sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The mass hangs from a joint at the crown and waves in the flow.
A sample snagged by the camera crawler is plant fibre, not fabric or plastic.
The joint is directly below a boulevard tree, and a fine root is visible entering the joint.
Upstream and downstream joints in the same run are clean and tight.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Fine roots entering at that joint have grown into the hanging mass
A mop head flushed from a home is caught at the joint
Grease has solidified into a hanging mass at the crown
The pipe crown has delaminated and is hanging into the flow

inference.explanation: The sample is plant fibre, a root is seen entering the joint below a tree, and neighbouring joints are clean. A mop would be fabric, grease forms on walls in flow, and delamination would be pipe material, not fibre.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the fibre source before cutting?

options.label: Grease sampling at the downstream restaurant
Pipe wall thickness testing along the whole run
Root cutter run with camera follow up at the same joint to inspect the joint opening

nextClue.explanation: Cutting with camera follow up both removes the mass and shows whether the joint opening is the entry point.

clueText.nc-a: There is no restaurant on this reach and the sample was plant fibre, not grease.
clueText.nc-b: Wall testing does not identify a fibre mass that sampling already showed is plant material.
clueText.nc-c: The cutter clears the mass and the follow up camera shows an open joint with fine roots at the gap.

tasks.prompt: Two homes at the low end of a court back up whenever the sewer is jetted from the upstream manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario court with a partial blockage. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Backups happen only during jetting, never during normal dry weather flow.
CCTV shows a dense root mass filling about half the pipe near the low end of the court.
When jetting stops, levels in the manhole fall back to normal within minutes.
Homes at the high end of the court never back up.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The jetting nozzle is spraying water directly into the home laterals
The homes have no backwater valves so any flow backs them up at all times
A downstream trunk collapse is holding back all flow at all times
Jetting water cannot pass the root restriction fast enough, so it surcharges to the low homes

inference.explanation: Backups only during jetting, a half full root mass at the low end, and rapid recovery when jetting stops all fit a restriction that passes normal flow but not jetting flow. A total downstream holdback would affect normal flow too.

nextClue.prompt: Which trial best confirms the restriction theory before root cutting?

options.label: Review rainfall records for the jetting days
Jet at reduced flow with a camera at the root mass and watch manhole levels during the trial
Install backwater valves in the two homes and jet at full flow

nextClue.explanation: A reduced flow trial with level watching tests whether flow rate through the restriction drives the surcharge, without flooding homes.

clueText.nc-a: The backups occur in dry weather during jetting, so rainfall is not the driver.
clueText.nc-b: At half jetting flow the manhole level stays normal and the camera shows water passing the root mass steadily.
clueText.nc-c: Valves protect homes but do not test what is restricting the main.

tasks.prompt: A root problem is suspected, but CCTV shows the main is clear while one home keeps backing up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario single home backup investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Main sewer CCTV for the full street is clear with no roots or debris.
The affected home backs up in dry weather while both neighbours drain normally.
A camera in the home lateral finds roots at a lateral joint 3 m from the house wall.
Dye flushed in the home reaches the main only after rodding the lateral.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The main is surcharged and pushing sewage into this one home
The home has a plumbing vent fault causing the backup
Roots in the private lateral, not the main, are causing this home backup
Roots in the main are blocking the whole street

inference.explanation: The main is clear on camera, neighbours drain normally, and roots are found in the lateral itself with dye delayed until rodding. A main problem would affect neighbours and appear on main CCTV.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents where responsibility for the repair lies?

options.label: Lateral camera log with distance from the house wall and the property line marked
Street CCTV report for the main
Rainfall log for the backup week

nextClue.explanation: A lateral log tied to the property line documents that the defect sits in the private lateral.

clueText.nc-a: The lateral log shows the root joint 3 m from the wall and 1 m inside the private side of the property line.
clueText.nc-b: The main report only confirms the main is clear, it does not locate the lateral defect.
clueText.nc-c: Rainfall is not involved in a dry weather single home backup.

tasks.prompt: After root cutting, flow improves for a day, then the same reach blocks again with soil and small stones in the returns.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario sewer after root cutting. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: First day returns after cutting are roots only and flow is restored.
Second day returns contain soil, sand, and small stones along with roots.
CCTV now shows an open displaced joint with soil visible behind the pipe wall.
A shallow depression has formed in the boulevard above the same joint.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Grit from upstream streets is settling at this joint
The joint has displaced and soil is entering the pipe, so the blockage is now structural
Roots alone regrew overnight and blocked the pipe again
The cutter left root debris that washed back into a ball

inference.explanation: Soil and stones in returns, soil visible behind an open displaced joint, and a surface depression all point to soil entry through a failed joint. Roots cannot regrow overnight, and upstream grit would not bring soil from behind the wall.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms soil entry before excavation is planned?

options.label: A second root cutting pass the next day
A grease sample from the downstream manhole
CCTV with the joint held in view while a dye and water test is run outside is not used, instead a still camera log of soil falling from the joint gap during flow

nextClue.explanation: Watching soil enter at the gap during flow directly confirms an open joint losing ground support.

clueText.nc-a: Another cutting pass treats roots, not soil entering through a displaced joint.
clueText.nc-b: Grease sampling does not test a joint that is visibly open with soil behind it.
clueText.nc-c: The camera log shows soil grains dropping from the joint gap as flow passes, matching the depression above.

tasks.prompt: Roots are heavy in a clay sewer, but one short section of newer plastic pipe in the same run has no roots at all.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario mixed material sewer run. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Clay sections show roots at most joints on CCTV.
The plastic section has fused, gasketed joints and shows no root entry.
Tree cover and soil conditions are the same over the whole run.
Flow and cleaning history are the same for both materials.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots enter through the open clay joints, and tight plastic joints deny them entry
The plastic pipe repels roots because of its smooth inner wall alone
Trees avoid the plastic section because it is newer
The camera missed roots in the plastic section because it moved faster there

inference.explanation: Same trees, soil, flow, and cleaning isolate joint type as the difference: open clay joints admit roots, tight joints do not. Smoothness alone does not explain entry at joints specifically.

nextClue.prompt: Which comparison best supports a joint sealing repair choice?

options.label: Jetting pressure records for the run
Joint by joint CCTV defect log comparing root entry at clay joints versus plastic joints
Tree species inventory for the street

nextClue.explanation: A joint by joint log ties root entry to joint condition, which is what a sealing repair must address.

clueText.nc-a: Jetting pressure was the same and does not explain entry at joints only.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows root entry at 14 of 16 clay joints and at none of the plastic joints in the same run.
clueText.nc-c: Tree species are the same over both sections, so an inventory cannot explain the contrast.

tasks.prompt: A sewer under a park blocks each spring and clears each fall with no cleaning done in between.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario park sewer with a seasonal pattern. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Blockages are reported in April and May in three separate years.
CCTV in June shows fresh pale root tips growing into the pipe at several joints.
CCTV the following January shows the same joints with much less root mass.
Rainfall in the blockage months is near normal and nearby streets do not block.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Spring rainfall inflow overloads this sewer each year
Park irrigation lines leak into the sewer each spring
Winter freezing blocks the pipe and spring thaw clears it
Seasonal root growth into the pipe peaks in spring and dies back by winter

inference.explanation: Fresh growing tips in June, dieback by January, and normal rainfall with clear neighbouring streets fit a growth cycle. Freezing would block in winter, the opposite of the observed pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the seasonal growth cycle for scheduling treatment?

options.label: CCTV from the same joints in spring, summer, and winter in one year, logged with dates
Park irrigation schedules
Frost depth records for the park

nextClue.explanation: Same joint dated images across seasons directly document growth and dieback for treatment timing.

clueText.nc-a: Dated images show pale new growth in May, a full mass in August, and a thin mass the next January.
clueText.nc-b: Irrigation schedules do not explain root tips seen growing at the joints.
clueText.nc-c: Frost records cannot explain blockages that peak in spring and clear by fall.

tasks.prompt: Rodding a blocked reach brings back roots mixed with pieces of orange clay pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario blocked clay sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Rod returns include root masses and curved orange clay fragments.
CCTV shows a section of pipe wall missing at the spring line with roots entering the hole.
The pipe is 60 year old clay in the affected section and sound clay elsewhere.
Soil is visible through the missing wall section.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Clay fragments came from a home lateral connection
The fragments are dried grease stained orange by sewage
The pipe wall has failed at that section and roots are entering through the break
Roots alone have grown thick enough to break the rodding cable

inference.explanation: Clay fragments in returns, a missing wall section on camera, and soil visible through the hole show a broken pipe, with roots using the break. Grease is not curved rigid fragments, and a lateral would not leave a hole in the main wall.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best defines the repair limits before digging?

options.label: A chemical root treatment of the whole reach
A flow study of the upstream catchment
Full CCTV of the reach with defect distances logged from both manholes

nextClue.explanation: A full defect log fixes the start and end of the failed section so excavation replaces only the failed length.

clueText.nc-a: Root treatment cannot restore a missing pipe wall.
clueText.nc-b: A flow study does not locate the limits of a broken section.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows sound pipe except for a 4 m failed section with the wall missing at the spring line.

tasks.prompt: A sewer reach cleaned on a fixed yearly schedule is found nearly clean at every visit, while another reach on a five year schedule blocks repeatedly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario cleaning schedule review. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The yearly reach carries free flowing sewage with no grease or root sources and is nearly clean each visit.
The five year reach sits below restaurants and has a flat grade, and blocks with grease between visits.
Moving the restaurant reach to a six month schedule for a trial ends its blockages.
Extending the clean reach to a three year schedule for a trial produces no problems there.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cleaning frequency should follow each reach condition and loading, not one fixed schedule for all
All reaches should stay on the yearly schedule regardless of condition
The restaurant reach blocks because crews clean it badly each time
The clean reach stays clean only because it is cleaned yearly

inference.explanation: Condition based trials prove the point both ways: more frequent cleaning cures the loaded flat reach, and less frequent cleaning harms nothing on the clean reach. A single fixed schedule cannot explain both trial results.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the schedule change?

options.label: Crew preference notes for the two reaches
The original yearly schedule document
Trial log with visit findings, blockage history, and the results at the new frequencies for both reaches

nextClue.explanation: Findings and blockage results at the trial frequencies are the evidence for condition based scheduling.

clueText.nc-a: Preferences do not show what the trial frequencies actually achieved.
clueText.nc-b: The original schedule is what the trial results show needs changing.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows no blockages at six months for the grease reach and no problems at three years for the clean reach.

tasks.prompt: A sewer below a row of restaurants backs up every few months and jetting returns are thick and pale yellow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario sewer serving restaurants. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Jetting returns are pale yellow, waxy chunks that float and smell of cooking oil.
CCTV shows a soft coating building from the walls inward, worst just downstream of the restaurant block.
Upstream of the restaurants the same pipe is clean on CCTV.
Problems ease for months after jetting, then slowly return.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Construction grit is washing in from a side street
Fats, oils, and grease from the food premises are coating and narrowing the pipe
Tree roots are growing in from the boulevard
The pipe has lost grade and solids are settling out

inference.explanation: Waxy floating returns, a wall coating worst below the restaurants, and a clean upstream pipe point to grease from the food premises. Roots would appear as fibres at joints, and lost grade would affect the upstream reach too.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best links the buildup to its source for follow up?

options.label: As built grade drawings for the street
CCTV comparison of the clean upstream reach and the coated reach below each food premises lateral
Tree inventory for the boulevard

nextClue.explanation: A paired upstream and downstream camera comparison ties the coating to the discharges between the two points.

clueText.nc-a: Drawings show design grade, not the coating that is narrowing the pipe today.
clueText.nc-b: The comparison shows a clean pipe above the first restaurant lateral and heavy coating below the last one.
clueText.nc-c: Trees are present along the whole street, including the clean upstream reach.

tasks.prompt: A lift station wet well and the sewer feeding it both foul with grease, but a second station on the same street stays clean.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario pair of lift stations on one street. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The fouling station serves a plaza with three take out restaurants.
The clean station serves only homes and a school.
Grease in the fouling station forms a floating mat that coats the level floats.
A grease interceptor at one restaurant is found full to the outlet when inspected.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Food premises grease, including a full interceptor passing grease onward, is fouling the one station
Both stations receive the same grease load and the clean one is just newer
The fouling station pumps are undersized and churn grease into a mat
Homes on the street are pouring cooking oil into drains

inference.explanation: Only the restaurant catchment fouls, the mat coats floats, and a full interceptor shows grease passing a control device. The clean station on the same street rules out a street wide home source.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the interceptor is passing grease?

options.label: Sample and depth check of the interceptor showing the grease layer at the outlet tee, with downstream manhole grease present
Pump run time comparison between the two stations
A survey of home cooking habits on the street

nextClue.explanation: Finding the grease layer at the outlet with grease downstream shows the device is no longer separating grease.

clueText.nc-a: Depths show grease filling to the outlet tee and the next manhole downstream carries matching grease chunks.
clueText.nc-b: Run times describe pumping, not whether an interceptor is separating grease.
clueText.nc-c: The clean station serves the homes, so home habits do not explain fouling at only the restaurant station.

tasks.prompt: Jetting a grease blocked sewer restores flow, but CCTV right after jetting shows the walls still coated and flow slow again in six weeks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario grease sewer cleaning check. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Immediately after jetting, CCTV shows a clean channel in the centre but thick grease still on the walls.
Six weeks later the channel has closed and backups return.
A scraping and collection run removes pails of grease and the next CCTV shows bare pipe walls.
After scraping, the reach stays clear for over a year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The grease is coming from a new source that started six weeks ago
The pipe collapsed after the first jetting and then healed
Roots regrew through the grease in six weeks
Jetting alone was cutting a channel through grease without removing it, so the cleaning method was ineffective

inference.explanation: Post jetting camera shows grease left on walls, rapid reclosure follows, and full removal by scraping gives a year of clear service. A new source or roots do not match the wall coating seen right after jetting.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best proves cleaning effectiveness for the maintenance plan?

options.label: Jetting truck hours for the reach
Count of backups in the six week period
Before and after CCTV pair for the same reach, one after jetting and one after scraping and collection

nextClue.explanation: A paired camera record shows what each method actually left on the walls, which sets the method choice.

clueText.nc-a: Truck hours measure effort, not the grease left behind on the walls.
clueText.nc-b: Backup counts show the problem returned, not which method removed the grease.
clueText.nc-c: The pair shows a greased wall after jetting and a bare wall after scraping, at the same chainage.

tasks.prompt: Grease blocks a sewer at a low flat section, but the same restaurants drain to a steeper sewer on the next street with no grease problem.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario comparison of two restaurant sewers. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both sewers receive grease from similar restaurants with similar interceptors.
The problem sewer runs at a very flat grade and flow is slow and deep.
The clear sewer runs steep and flow is fast and shallow.
CCTV shows grease coating only in the flat sewer, starting where the grade flattens.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The flat sewer has root entry that the steep sewer lacks
The steep sewer is cleaned weekly and the flat one is never cleaned
Grease is depositing where slow flat flow lets it cool and stick, not only because of the load
The flat street restaurants discharge far more grease than the steep street

inference.explanation: Similar loads and interceptors, with coating starting exactly where grade flattens, point to deposition in slow flow. No roots are reported on camera, and no cleaning difference is stated.

nextClue.prompt: Which measurement best confirms the deposition explanation?

options.label: Root defect log for the flat sewer
Velocity check in both sewers at similar flow, paired with the CCTV coating start point
Interceptor size comparison for both streets

nextClue.explanation: Matching velocity to the coating start point tests whether slow flow is where grease drops out.

clueText.nc-a: No root defects were seen on the flat sewer camera run.
clueText.nc-b: Velocity in the flat reach is well below the steep reach at similar flow, and coating starts at the flattening point.
clueText.nc-c: Interceptors are already stated as similar, so sizing does not explain the contrast.

tasks.prompt: A home reports a sewer backup and the crew finds solid white fat in the home lateral and in the main at the connection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario single home backup with fat found. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The fat in the lateral is fresh, soft, and smells of recent cooking.
The main at the connection is coated but still flowing, and neighbours drain normally.
The home reports frying large meals daily and pouring pan fat into the sink.
After the lateral is cleared, the home drains normally while the main coating remains.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Tree roots filled the lateral with fat covered roots
The home own discharge blocked its lateral, while the main coating is not yet blocking flow
The main is fully blocked and backing up into this home only
A city grease mat in the main sealed the lateral outlet

inference.explanation: Neighbours drain normally, the main still flows, fresh fat fills the lateral, and clearing the lateral alone restores the home. A blocked main would affect neighbours and clearing the lateral would not fix it.

nextClue.prompt: Which advice check best confirms the source for the follow up visit?

options.label: A simple kitchen practice review with the resident plus a short lateral camera check showing no other defect
A full street CCTV survey
A manhole surcharge record for the street

nextClue.explanation: Reviewing the discharge practice plus confirming the lateral has no other defect closes the source question.

clueText.nc-a: The review confirms pan fat goes to the sink and the camera shows a clean lateral with no roots or breaks.
clueText.nc-b: The street main is already known to be flowing with neighbours draining normally.
clueText.nc-c: No surcharge was reported by neighbours on the street.

tasks.prompt: Grease problems in a downtown sewer get worse every winter and ease every summer with the same restaurant load.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario downtown sewer with a seasonal grease pattern. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Restaurant count and interceptor service records are unchanged across the year.
Winter CCTV shows hard, thick grease deposits, summer CCTV shows thin soft deposits.
Sewage temperature in the sewer is several degrees lower in winter.
Flow volumes are similar in winter and summer.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cold sewage in winter hardens grease deposits, so the same load causes worse narrowing
Restaurants discharge more grease in winter than in summer
Roots grow into the sewer in winter and die in summer
Infiltration in winter dilutes flow and drops solids in this reach

inference.explanation: Load, service records, and flow are steady while sewage temperature and deposit hardness change with season. That fits temperature hardening, not a load change or a winter root cycle, which is the reverse of root growth.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports scheduling winter cleaning for this reach?

options.label: Restaurant sales records by month
Tree growth records for downtown
Seasonal CCTV and sewage temperature log for the same reach over one full year

nextClue.explanation: Pairing deposit thickness with sewage temperature over a year documents the cold hardening pattern.

clueText.nc-a: Sales records do not measure what hardened inside the pipe.
clueText.nc-b: Roots grow most in warm seasons, the opposite of this pattern.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows deposits thickest and hardest when sewage is coldest, with the same premises discharging.

tasks.prompt: A sewer serving a food processing plant blocks with a pale solid that looks like grease, but it does not melt in hot water like grease does.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario industrial sewer investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The solid is pale and waxy but stays solid in hot water that melts a grease sample from a restaurant sewer.
The plant recently changed to a cleaning product with a high mineral oil and wax content.
Upstream of the plant lateral the sewer is clean, downstream it is coated.
Laboratory screening of the solid matches wax and mineral oil, with little food fat.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The blockage is ordinary food grease that has gone hard with age
The blockage is cement grout washed in from construction
The blockage is root mass bleached pale by sewage
The blockage is wax and mineral oil from the plant process change, not food grease

inference.explanation: Hot water behaviour and lab screening separate wax from food fat, and the clean upstream pipe ties it to the plant that changed products. Grout would be hard mineral, not waxy, and roots are fibrous.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the plant source for the discharge follow up?

options.label: Construction permits near the plant
Paired samples, plant lateral discharge and pipe deposit, with matching lab screening results
Hot water test alone on one deposit sample

nextClue.explanation: Matching the discharge to the deposit by lab screening is the direct source link.

clueText.nc-a: No construction is stated near the plant, and grout does not match the waxy lab result.
clueText.nc-b: Both samples screen as wax and mineral oil with little food fat, matching the new cleaning product.
clueText.nc-c: One hot water test suggests wax but does not tie the deposit to the plant discharge.

tasks.prompt: Crews find grease only in the first 20 m below a manhole, and the rest of a long reach is clean.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario long sewer reach with localised grease. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Grease coats the first 20 m below the upstream manhole, then the pipe runs clean for 180 m.
A food truck commissary lateral enters at that same manhole.
Flow from the commissary is discharged in large warm batches at washdown time.
Grease thickness fades with distance below the manhole rather than growing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The cleaning crew only cleaned the lower 180 m and left the top dirty
A sag in the first 20 m collects grease from the whole catchment
Grease enters at the manhole from the commissary lateral and deposits as its batch flow cools
Grease is carried evenly along the whole reach from many homes

inference.explanation: Grease fading with distance below one entry point, batch washdown at that point, and a clean lower reach fit a single nearby source depositing as it cools. An even home source would coat more evenly, and a sag is not stated.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the commissary as the entry point?

options.label: Manhole inspection during washdown, watching the lateral discharge and grease arriving with it
A catchment wide survey of home kitchens
A level survey of the full 200 m reach

nextClue.explanation: Watching the discharge arrive at washdown directly links timing, entry point, and grease.

clueText.nc-a: At washdown the lateral runs warm and milky and fresh grease appears at the manhole while other laterals run clear.
clueText.nc-b: A home survey cannot explain grease that fades within 20 m of one lateral.
clueText.nc-c: A level survey checks grade, not which lateral delivers the grease.

tasks.prompt: A grease interceptor program starts and sewer backups on the street fall sharply within a year, except at one address.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario street after a grease control program. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: All restaurants on the street joined the program and service their interceptors on schedule.
Backups stopped at every restaurant block except the block below one bakery.
The bakery is classed as food premises but was not included because it bakes off site mixes.
CCTV below the bakery shows fresh grease coating while other reaches stay clean.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots took over the bakery reach after grease was reduced
The one premises left out of the program is still discharging grease and causing the remaining backups
The program failed and backups continue everywhere at the old rate
The bakery block pipe collapsed in the same year

inference.explanation: Backups stopped everywhere except below the one excluded premises, where fresh grease is seen. That pattern fits a remaining source, not program failure, collapse, or roots, none of which are observed.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the bakery discharge before it is added to the program?

options.label: A street wide backup count for the year
A tree survey for the bakery block
CCTV above and below the bakery lateral plus a look at its washdown discharge

nextClue.explanation: Camera above and below the lateral isolates what the bakery adds to the pipe.

clueText.nc-a: Street counts show where backups remain, not which premises adds the grease.
clueText.nc-b: No roots were reported on the bakery reach camera.
clueText.nc-c: The pipe is clean above the bakery lateral and freshly coated below it, and washdown runs milky.
